To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of people in our survey (over 90 per cent of the respondents) listen to music in their daily lives.

'listening to music' is a broad and multifaceted activity, which can be understood in many different ways; the activity of listening is not limited to music, as it can include listening to other types of sounds; and the activity of listening to music can be understood from a variety of perspectives, such as psychological, neurological, sociological, anthropological and historical.
listening to music is an activity that involves people, practices, and experiences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and cultural contexts in which people engage in listening to music.
the ways in which people engage with music and how they make sense of their experiences of music, in a variety of settings and in a variety of ways.
the experience and meaning of listening, with the practices and activities of listeners and with the ways in which these are affected by the contexts in which they take place.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
listening to music is a complex and multifaceted experience.
the study of listening to music is a complex, multifaceted and interdisciplinary endeavour.
there are as many approaches to the study of listening as there are approaches to the study and analysis of music.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how people listen to music and what they do while they do it.

we are interested in how people make music and how music is used in society.5 We have chosen to focus on the listening experience because we believe that listening is a crucial element in the relationship between people and music.
we have drawn on the work of all these groups, but with an emphasis on the work of anthropologists, ethno-musicologists and social and cultural historians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a great deal of overlap between the approaches used and the kinds of questions asked in the various disciplines that study listening.
listening is a social practice, and one that is shaped and reshaped by the social contexts in which it takes place.
listening is a complex activity.
